messages:
pagerbot: INCIDENT alert — KV cache growth spike on eu-west-1 inference fleet. error-rate bump + latency tail. pager: paging oncall devon at 2415006789 :rotating_light:

devon (oncall-runtime): on it. looking at the dashboards now. any customer reports yet?

sophia (support): we have one escalation from ACME/Payments on increased 500s for invoice-generation flows. they sent logs showing tokenized prompt length ~8k tokens.

devon (oncall-runtime): copy, thanks. initial hypothesis: continuous batching + large prefixes triggered huge KV cache entries (prefix keys ~50KB). seeing sustained write rate to redis-kv-shards-4.

maria (sre): I'm seeing the same. KV memory per shard jumped from 8GB -> 38GB in 6m. eviction rate not keeping up due to persistent TTL=never on some prefixes.

raj (eng-runtime): new batch config rolled out 3h ago to increase max_batch_window to 120ms and enable aggressive prefetch for long contexts. might be related.

devon (oncall-runtime): ok rollback plan: revert batch window and prefetch flag on runtime config to last-known-good. preparing hotfix now.

ops-bot: Deploy triggered by devon: rollback config -> runtime-config/v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0. Start: 2415007000.

devon (oncall-runtime): running `redwood rollout set runtime-config --name=batch_window --value=40 --env=eu-west-1` and disabling `prefetch_long_contexts=true`

maria (sre): also recommend setting a safety TTL on prefix entries while we stabilize: `redis-cli --cluster call shards EXPIREPREFIX 3600` (dry-run first).

raj (eng-runtime): note: there was also a prompt template change in templates/invoice_v2 introduced yesterday that adds a long system prompt for customers >1k tokens. tokenizer fingerprint changed? Could be causing wider prefix variety -> cache fragmentation.

sophia (support): ACME confirmed degradation started ~10:12 UTC and matched our timeline. they temporarily rolled back to invoice_v1 and errors dropped.

devon (oncall-runtime): hotfix applied, prefetch disabled, batch window = 40ms. ops-bot reports config rollout success to 80% of pods. monitoring for recovery.

ops-bot: Config rollout status: 80% -> 100% at 2415007320.

maria (sre): after config changes, KV write rate dropped 7x. memory usage trending down. eviction rate back to normal.

devon (oncall-runtime): running targeted purge for known problematic prefixes from yesterday: `redwood cache purge --prefix="invoice_v2:" --env=eu-west-1 --confirm` (will wait 30s for approvals)

raj (eng-runtime): hold on purge for 30s — need to coordinate with ACME rollback to avoid double-retries.

sophia (support): ACME is aware; they asked us to proceed once we confirm rollback success. they prefer we purge the stale prefixes.

devon (oncall-runtime): purging now. command output: ```
INFO: scanning keys matching invoice_v2:*
Found 12,342 keys
Purging 12,342 keys... done
```

maria (sre): good. verify redis shard stability. no longer seeing long GC pauses.

pagerbot: Incident created: INC-2415. Severity: P1 -> P2 (customer impact contained).

devon (oncall-runtime): initial customer impact: ~3% of requests for long-context generation returned 500 or timed out during peak. ACME saw ~8% error rate on invoice flows. We mitigated by rolling back template and applying config rollback.

raj (eng-runtime): root cause theory: combined effect of (1) template change creating many unique long prefixes (tokenizer produced different hashes than invoice_v1 because of trailing unicode/whitespace) + (2) longer batch window + prefetch caused inflight requests to generate extra cache keys and large KV entries. tokenizer mismatch amplified key cardinality.

maria (sre): action items for immediate 24h: 
- enforce prefix TTL default for all new prefixes (3600s)
- add a guardrail in runtime to refuse prefetch for requests > 4k tokens unless explicit opt-in
- add a metric for distinct prefix cardinality per minute

devon (oncall-runtime): I'll open PR to add TTL in runtime caching layer and revert batch window prod config permanently.

raj (eng-runtime): I'll reproduce locally with invoice_v2 template + new tokenizer commit hash to confirm fingerprint drift. sharing repro steps in the ticket.

sophia (support): I created a customer postmortem draft for ACME and CC'd their engineering lead.

maria (sre): tagging oncall handoff: I'll take next 2 hours then hand to raj for deep-dive. devon, schedule postmortem meeting.

devon (oncall-runtime): taking notes. summary for ops log: `cache_pulse_2415006789` — cause: config+template interaction -> mitigation: config rollback, prefix purge, TTL guard.

ops-bot: Noted. Creating follow-up ticket INC-2415-BIS: assign @raj, @devon, @maria.

raj (eng-runtime): follow-up: also want to audit tokenizer changes — possible strip/normalize whitespace regression. will compare token counts across versions and run mapreduce of prefixes by hash length.

sophia (support): ACME acknowledged interim report and is ok with full postmortem timeline. they requested ETA on permanent fix for TTL guard.

devon (oncall-runtime): ETA 48h for TTL guard PR review + canary. will mark in ticket.

maria (sre): closing P1 escalation, leaving incident channel open for postmortem. final status: system stable, customer degraded but functional, purge completed.

pagerbot: Incident INC-2415 status changed to monitoring at 2415008921.

devon (oncall-runtime): thanks team. follow-up reminders: add unit tests for tokenizer normalization, and add integration test that simulates large-prefix workloads.

sophia (support): will coordinate customer comms and share final postmortem draft once PRs land. :white_check_mark:
